dockerfile
# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its wide package support and stability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build and install Kripke.
# It minimizes layer count, reducing the final image size.
RUN \
    # 1. Update package lists and install build-time and run-time dependencies.
    # - build-essential, cmake, git: Required for compiling the source code.
    # - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Provide the MPI library for parallel execution.
    # - ca-certificates: Required for secure network connections (e.g., git clone).
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        g++ \
        git \
        libopenmpi-dev \
        openmpi-bin \
        ca-certificates && \
    \
    # 2. Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
    # These settings prevent common issues with network interface detection and
    # CPU affinity when running inside cgroups-restricted containers.
    echo "btl_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "hwloc_base_binding_policy = none" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = slot" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    \
    # 3. Clone the Kripke repository from the main branch.
    # A shallow clone (--depth 1) is used to reduce download size.
    git clone --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke && \
    \
    # 4. Configure and build Kripke.
    # - A separate build directory is created to keep source clean.
    # - -DENABLE_MPI=ON is crucial for enabling MPI support.
    # - make -j$(nproc) uses all available CPU cores to speed up compilation.
    cd /opt/kripke && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake -DENABLE_MPI=ON .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # 5. Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This makes the 'kripke' command available system-wide.
    cp ./bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    \
    # 6. Clean up to minimize the final image size.
    # - Remove the source code directory.
    # - Purge build-time dependencies that are not needed at runtime.
    # - Clean apt caches.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke && \
    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove build-essential cmake git libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default command for the container to display Kripke's help message.
# This makes the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its wide package support and stability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build and install Kripke.
# It minimizes layer count, reducing the final image size.
RUN \
    # 1. Update package lists and install build-time and run-time dependencies.
    # - build-essential, cmake, git: Required for compiling the source code.
    # - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Provide the MPI library for parallel execution.
    # - ca-certificates: Required for secure network connections (e.g., git clone).
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        g++ \
        git \
        libopenmpi-dev \
        openmpi-bin \
        ca-certificates && \
    \
    # 2. Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
    # These settings prevent common issues with network interface detection and
    # CPU affinity when running inside cgroups-restricted containers.
    echo "btl_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "hwloc_base_binding_policy = none" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = slot" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    \
    # 3. Clone the Kripke repository from the master branch.
    # FIX: Changed branch from 'main' to 'master' as the 'main' branch does not exist.
    # A shallow clone (--depth 1) is used to reduce download size.
    git clone --depth 1 --branch master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke && \
    \
    # 4. Configure and build Kripke.
    # - A separate build directory is created to keep source clean.
    # - -DENABLE_MPI=ON is crucial for enabling MPI support.
    # - make -j$(nproc) uses all available CPU cores to speed up compilation.
    cd /opt/kripke && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake -DENABLE_MPI=ON .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # 5. Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This makes the 'kripke' command available system-wide.
    cp ./bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    \
    # 6. Clean up to minimize the final image size.
    # - Remove the source code directory.
    # - Purge build-time dependencies that are not needed at runtime.
    # - Clean apt caches.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke && \
    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove build-essential cmake git libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default command for the container to display Kripke's help message.
# This makes the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# Use Ubuntu 22.04 as the base image for its wide package support and stability.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build and install Kripke.
# It minimizes layer count, reducing the final image size.
RUN \
    # 1. Update package lists and install build-time and run-time dependencies.
    # - build-essential, cmake, git: Required for compiling the source code.
    # - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Provide the MPI library for parallel execution.
    # - ca-certificates: Required for secure network connections (e.g., git clone).
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        g++ \
        git \
        libopenmpi-dev \
        openmpi-bin \
        ca-certificates && \
    \
    # 2. Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
    # These settings prevent common issues with network interface detection and
    # CPU affinity when running inside cgroups-restricted containers.
    echo "btl_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "hwloc_base_binding_policy = none" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = slot" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    \
    # 3. Clone the Kripke repository and its submodules from the main branch.
    # FIX: Added '--recursive' to fetch the 'blt' submodule required by CMake.
    # FIX: Changed branch back to 'main' as specified in the original request.
    # A shallow clone (--depth 1) is used to reduce download size.
    git clone --recursive --depth 1 --branch main https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke && \
    \
    # 4. Configure and build Kripke.
    # - A separate build directory is created to keep source clean.
    # - -DENABLE_MPI=ON is crucial for enabling MPI support.
    # - make -j$(nproc) uses all available CPU cores to speed up compilation.
    cd /opt/kripke && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake -DENABLE_MPI=ON .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # 5. Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # This makes the 'kripke' command available system-wide.
    cp ./bin/kripke /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    \
    # 6. Clean up to minimize the final image size.
    # - Remove the source code directory.
    # - Purge build-time dependencies that are not needed at runtime.
    # - Clean apt caches.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke && \
    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove build-essential cmake git libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default command for the container to display Kripke's help message.
# This makes the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

    # - build-essential, cmake, git: Required for compiling the source code.
    # - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Provide the MPI library for parallel execution.
    # - ca-certificates: Required for secure network connections (e.g., git clone).
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        g++ \
        git \
        libopenmpi-dev \
        openmpi-bin \
        ca-certificates && \
    \
    # 2. Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.

    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "hwloc_base_binding_policy = none" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = slot" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \

    \

    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a non-interactive frontend for package managers to prevent prompts during build.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# This single RUN command performs all necessary steps to build and install Kripke.
# It minimizes layer count, reducing the final image size.
RUN \
    # 1. Update package lists and install build-time and run-time dependencies.
    # - build-essential, cmake, git: Required for compiling the source code.
    # - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: Provide the MPI library for parallel execution.
    # - ca-certificates: Required for secure network connections (e.g., git clone).
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        g++ \
        git \
        libopenmpi-dev \
        openmpi-bin \
        ca-certificates && \
    \
    # 2. Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
    # These settings prevent common issues with network interface detection and
    # CPU affinity when running inside cgroups-restricted containers.
    echo "btl_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "oob_tcp_if_exclude = lo,docker0" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "hwloc_base_binding_policy = none" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "rmaps_base_mapping_policy = slot" >> /etc/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    \
    # 3. Clone the Kripke repository and its submodules from the default branch.
    # The repository's default branch is 'master'.
    # A shallow clone (--depth 1) is used to reduce download size.
    git clone --recursive --depth 1 --branch master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke && \
    \
    # 4. Configure and build Kripke.
    # - A separate build directory is created to keep source clean.
    # - -DENABLE_MPI=ON is crucial for enabling MPI support.
    # - make -j$(nproc) uses all available CPU cores to speed up compilation.
    cd /opt/kripke && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake -DENABLE_MPI=ON .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # 5. Copy the compiled executable to a standard system location on the PATH.
    # FIX: The build process creates 'kripke.exe', so copy from that source file.
    # The destination is 'kripke' to provide a standard command name on the PATH.
    cp ./bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    \
    # 6. Clean up to minimize the final image size.
    # - Remove the source code directory.
    # - Purge build-time dependencies that are not needed at runtime.
    # - Clean apt caches.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke && \
    apt-get purge -y --auto-remove build-essential cmake git libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the default command for the container to display Kripke's help message.
# This makes the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

flux-minicluster-manifest
# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke HPC application using the Flux Operator.
# The previous run failed due to an invalid problem decomposition specified in the command arguments.
# This version corrects the issue by reverting to running kripke with no parameters, as instructed.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster deployment.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The job will be deployed to the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster's IndexedJob.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks for the flux run command, targeting the c7a.12xlarge instance.
  tasks: 48
  # Pods will not be deleted after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Schedule the pod on a specific AWS AMD-based (x86) instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "c7a.12xlarge"
  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - # The command is simplified to run kripke with no parameters to resolve the previous assertion failure.
      command: kripke
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the job submitter.
      launcher: false
  # Specify settings for the Flux Operator's logging.
  logging:
    # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke HPC application using the Flux Operator.
# The previous attempt failed with an "Assertion Failed: Number of MPI ranks must match decomposition" error.
# This was because the application, when run with no arguments, defaults to expecting 1 process,
# but the MiniCluster was configured for 48 tasks.
# This manifest corrects the issue by explicitly telling Kripke to decompose the problem
# across the 48 tasks provided by Flux, using the --procs argument (4 * 4 * 3 = 48).
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster deployment.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The job will be deployed to the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster's IndexedJob.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks for the flux run command.
  tasks: 48
  # Pods will not be deleted after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Schedule the pod on a specific AWS AMD-based (x86) instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "c7a.12xlarge"
  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - # Corrected command to align the application's process grid with the spec.tasks count.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,3 --niter 10 --zones 64,64,64 --groups 32 --dset 16
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the job submitter.
      launcher: false
  # Specify settings for the Flux Operator's logging.
  logging:
    # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

# Previous attempts failed due to incorrect command-line arguments causing assertion errors within Kripke.
# The core instruction is to revert to a parameter-less command, letting the application use its default decomposition logic.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster deployment.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The job will be deployed to the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster's IndexedJob.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks for the flux run command.
  tasks: 48
  # Pods will not be deleted after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Schedule the pod on a specific AWS AMD-based (x86) instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "c7a.12xlarge"
  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - # Reverting to a command with no parameters as instructed to resolve prior failures.
      command: kripke
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the job submitter.
      launcher: false
  # Specify settings for the Flux Operator's logging.
  logging:
    # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

  containers:
    - # Corrected command to match the application's process decomposition to the task count.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,3 --niter 10 --zones 64,64,64 --groups 32 --dset 16
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the job submitter.
      launcher: false
  # Specify settings for the Flux Operator's logging.
  logging:
    # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke HPC application using the Flux Operator.
# The previous run failed with an "Assertion Failed: Number of zones in Z must evenly divide into the number of subdomains".
# This was caused by a mismatch between the process grid Z-dimension (3 from --procs 4,4,3) and the zones Z-dimension (64 from --zones 64,64,64), as 64 is not divisible by 3.
# This manifest corrects the issue by changing the zones to 96,96,96, as 96 is divisible by both 4 and 3.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster deployment.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The job will be deployed to the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster's IndexedJob.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks for the flux run command.
  tasks: 48
  # Pods will not be deleted after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Schedule the pod on a specific AWS AMD-based (x86) instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "c7a.12xlarge"
  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - # Corrected command with a valid zone decomposition for the specified process grid.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,3 --niter 10 --zones 96,96,96 --groups 32 --dset 16
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the job submitter.
      launcher: false
  # Specify settings for the Flux Operator's logging.
  logging:
    # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke HPC application using the Flux Operator.
# The previous single-task run was inefficient and terminated unexpectedly. This version is corrected
# to run in parallel, utilizing all available vCPUs on the node.
# The `tasks` count is set to 16 to match the vCPUs of the r7iz.8xlarge instance.
# Crucially, the `--procs` argument is added to the Kripke command to ensure the application's
# internal problem decomposition (2*2*4=16) matches the number of MPI ranks launched by Flux.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster deployment.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The job will be deployed to the default namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster's IndexedJob.
  # Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Set tasks to 16 to fully utilize the vCPUs of the r7iz.8xlarge instance.
  tasks: 16
  # Pods will not be deleted after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # Pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Schedule the pod on a specific memory-optimized, Intel-based AWS instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "r7iz.8xlarge"
  # Define the application container.
  containers:
    - # Command updated with --procs to match the parallel execution of 16 tasks.
      command: kripke --procs 2,2,4 --niter 10 --zones 48,48,48 --groups 32 --dset 16
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # This container is a worker, not the job submitter.
      launcher: false
  # Specify settings for the Flux Operator's logging.
  logging:
    # Enforce strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

Decision 3: RETRY

Agent's Rationale: Previous attempts with high core counts and large problem sizes on both ARM and AMD architectures resulted in very poor performance, likely due to memory bandwidth or cache saturation issues. This attempt pivots to an Intel instance known for high clock speeds and an extremely high memory-to-CPU ratio (r7iz.8xlarge). The task count and problem size are scaled down to match the 16 cores, aiming to establish a strong performance baseline on high-quality cores before attempting to scale up again.

Decision 4: RETRY

Agent's Rationale: All previous attempts at scaling to multiple processes, regardless of architecture (ARM, AMD, Intel), resulted in a figure of merit an order of magnitude worse than the initial single-task baseline. This indicates that for this application on a single node, MPI overhead is severely degrading performance. This attempt reverts to the successful single-task strategy, but moves to a high-performance Intel instance (r7iz.8xlarge) and moderately increases the problem size to increase the work done, aiming to improve the numerator of the FOM calculation without incurring ruinous scaling costs.

This attempt keeps the promising single-task approach on the same fast `r7iz.8xlarge` instance but reduces the problem size (`--zones` from 64 to 48) to ensure completion and establish a strong performance baseline.

Decision 6: STOP

Agent's Rationale: After multiple attempts, it is clear that for this application on a single node, MPI scaling is detrimental. All multi-process runs and single-process runs with larger problem sizes resulted in a Figure of Merit an order of magnitude worse than the initial baseline. The optimal configuration is the simplest one: a single task running the default problem size. This configuration is submitted as the final, optimized result on a high-performance Intel instance to maximize single-core speed.
